utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that. You said, and let me remind you, you said that Drago Prcac came to you and asked you to film a story about Omarska. That's what I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Just be more precise in your questions. This was sometime after Drago had retired. So this must have been in 1986 or 1987, after Drago retired. In a conversation, he said that the people in Omarska have a very good football club and that we could make a feature about them. And as far as I can remember, as far as I can recollect and collect my thoughts to that period, the story was about the water supply problems that Omarska was having, which were very serious at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: And the second feature?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, one was about the local football club and the other one was about the problems with the water supply for the inhabitants of Omarska. He suggested that we go there, and we did. We made these two stories about the life of the inhabitants of Omarska. Drago Prcac was not present when we were filming.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who was present?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was; my assistant, Burho Kapetanovic, who was killed in the Omarska camp; and Boro Grubic, a journalist, a reporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: So you made two features, one about the football club. Did you interview anyone?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When making the sports feature, as far as I can remember, we had an interview with the coach.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Will you please answer the questions I'm asking? Who did you interview?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we interviewed the coach of the Omarksa football club. I think his name was Tatic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you filmed the other feature about the water supply problems, who did you interview?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think it was the secretary of the neighbourhood community and his name was Zrnic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who were you working for at the time, which television?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time it was called Television Sarajevo. Today it is called the Television of Bosnia-Herzegovina, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovan Simic, it is true that the witness mentioned these features in the examination-in-chief, but I think these events took place in 1986/1987. They are quite outside the indictment. Do you really need to pursue the matter? They're absolutely outside the indictment in terms of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is true, these are events outside the relevant period, but these are events that the witness claims took place, and my client and myself think that it never took place. So we're claim that this feature was never filmed, never made. It may have been made but not at the request of Mr. Prcac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you trying to call in question the credibility of the witness? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where was this feature shown, broadcast? Was it at all broadcast?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on Sarajevo television.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after it was filmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you tell the football club or the other people to watch that story on television?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My principle -- no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether Mr. Prcac was a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said something else, so could you explain why you said that. On what ground did you come to the conclusion that everybody respected Mr. Prcac? Or let me put it differently. Was he a party official?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was he a wealthy man?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he have a car, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had an old Golf, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was it registered in his name? Did he drive it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, perhaps. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he have a car or not?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he had an old Golf.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, why did you come to the conclusion that he was respected?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the tradition in our part of the world the people for -- the people working in the police to be respected. The greatest respect is given to the priest, and then the policeman, also a forester, a postman, all people working in state services.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Tell me, who is Slavisa Djukanovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavisa is an acquaintance of many years. Until 1992, he worked as a photographer in the work organisation called Bosna Montaza. When the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina occurred and the events in Prijedor, he put on a uniform and worked for the Serb television.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: What is he by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know where he is now?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you see Slavisa Djukanovic and Mr. Prcac together in Omarksa, and when?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you ever before see them together or was that the first time?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first time I saw them. I didn't see them together before.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, please, after your arrest, did you see Drago Prcac in the camp immediately?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which arrest, the first or second?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: The second.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second? No, I didn't see him immediately because I spent seven days in the garage. So I didn't leave the garage for seven days, because the first time I went out I was beaten, and I didn't dare go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said that you saw him more often in the second half of July.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more often in the second half of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you see Zeljko Meakic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he differ from the others?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: So you saw him often?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where did he move around?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everywhere in the camp. Even his car, which had been stolen somewhere, a green Mercedes --

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Will you please answer just my question. You said that Drago was a deputy. Whose deputy was he?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zeljko Meakic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was Ranko Mijic's position then?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ranko Mijic was head of the team of investigators working in the Omarska camp and even of the team of investigators that worked in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said that you came to the conclusion that Drago was a deputy because he approved movement of detainees from one room to another.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only because that, because all the problems that occurred in the second half of July and the beginning of August, until we were transferred to Trnopolje, all the administrative things were taken care of by Drago Prcac.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: So according to you, in the second half of July, Drago Prcac was deputy and in charge of administrative affairs?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else. Was he the oldest person in the camp among the camp personnel?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who was older?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the guards.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Jovan Simic.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was among the oldest. I think there were several guards who were perhaps older, who looked older.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know Azedin Oklopcic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know Abdulah Brkic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know Rezak Hukanovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I know him, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, your sister was in the camp as well?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: She was in the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: She could see from the restaurant through the glass the events on the pista?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you have a problem with water? With water?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was there a truck with a water tank often the pista?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, this truck would bring water only for the guards and the camp personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: But was there this truck or some container or anything on the pista?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to your sister about the events in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very rarely, because my sister doesn't wish to be reminded of that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to any other woman from the camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps with one of my acquaintances that I knew before going to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: What about Sifeta Susic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Sifeta Susic very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you see her after going to the camp? Did you visit her?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe once.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to the incident with Rizo Hadzalic. You described that incident in some detail. Was Rizo sitting or standing just before that incident?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rizo and Goran were standing. They had just been brought to the place from where they were supposed to be taken for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were they eating anything?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that. But later I learnt that one of the detainees coming back from the restaurant gave Rizo a piece of bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you, you already have the version in Serbian of your statement from the 12th to the 16th of November, 1994, which, as my learned friend has already established, you read and signed. Would you look at page 27, please? And I should like to remind you -- 27, third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have page 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: I apologise. The page is 19. I'm sorry, the page is 19. Third paragraph. You said, "Rizo Hadzalic, Goran Kardum, Asif Kapetanovic, Dzevad Grozdanic and Cmil Pezo. I saw that Rizo and Goran had been killed. Someone threw them some bread and someone said bon apetite. They used a Muslim word to ask the person to join them. A guard heard and they were beaten to death. Rizo died on the pista." Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: On the same page, the first paragraph, last sentence, let me remind you. "I asked to go on the pista, the best place, because you could breathe there, and there was a truck with a water tank standing there. There was a water tank there." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I wrote that, and when I asked to go to the pista, thinking that the water tank was for us, but it was only for the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: But you gave this statement after you left the camp.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but I am telling you there was a water tank but we didn't use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was there a water tank or not?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was somewhere over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: It was not on the pista?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the pista but on the opposite side, and it was used by the guards. We didn't take that water. We drank polluted water.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: What did you call the pista? Was it the area between restaurant and the hangar? Were there pots for plants there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pauses, please, Mr. Jovan Simic, otherwise we just can't follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: On that pista, was there a water tank? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: So on the pista, between the restaurant and the hangar, which was marked with flower pots?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not there, because the entire asphalt area was called by us by the pista, because it was asphalt, but more specifically, when you say "the pista" --

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Was Rizo Hadzalic perhaps standing again the restaurant wall?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was, but he wasn't facing the restaurant wall, as far as I can remember, because he had only just been brought there.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Which restaurant wall?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said next to the pillar.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Left of the pillar, next to the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: He wasn't next to the other wall of the restaurant, which continues and becomes the glass wall?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: And he wasn't sitting and he wasn't eating?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Would you tell me who you were with in Mujo's room, as we don't have much time. Was Mr. Rezak Hukanovic in that room?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I spent a lot of time on the pista, I don't remember if he was in Mujo's room because there were more than 700 of us at one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: One more question. Somebody was in charge of the room. First it was Mujo and then Burho?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: And who was the third person? Was it perhaps Avledin [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't Avledin.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: From this semi-circular glass above the entrance, when you're on the pista, when you're standing in that area, glassed-in area, did you see the whole pista?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no occasion to look at the pista from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Can you see the entrance to the restaurant from there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: You assume so but you don't know.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I was never there.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know or do you not know? Is it possible to see the entrance to the restaurant from this semi-circular glass area?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me yes or no.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was never there in that glassed-in area, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just one more thing. Is it true that during the last seven or ten days the conditions in the camp improved? Could you explain that? Did conditions in the camp improve during the last seven or ten days?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, that is not correct. Perhaps the last day or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Something else, please. As far as Zeljko Meakic is concerned, you said you saw him frequently.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: That he wore a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: How did you come to the conclusion that he was the camp commander?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he behaved in such a way, a man who issued orders to everyone, not just to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he give orders to Drago Prcac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but when he was absent, then it was Drago Prcac.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you see Drago giving orders to someone?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: To whom?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I have no further questions. I'm sorry, Your Honour, just one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: You gave several statements. When you came to The Hague, did you make another statement to the investigator, a new statement?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to the Prosecutors when you came to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: This time, when did you come?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, did you talk to the Prosecution during the last five days?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. We did talk about the court proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Jovan Simic. Mr. Krstan Simic, if you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sivac.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: From what the Presiding Judge has already said, you have already heard my name. My name is Krstan Simic. I am from Banja Luka. I have only three very brief questions for you. Let me first check if I have correctly understood you while you were answering questions by Mr. Jovan Simic. You stated that after your second arrest, you spent some time in the garage before the interrogation and that you went outside only on one occasion during that time, that you were beaten up, and that you never went outside before the interrogation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the garage you were taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken to the first room on the left-hand side, and this is where encountered my old acquaintances Neso Babic and Neso Tomcic, who used to work as investigators in the Prijedor SUP for a number years with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said you were not beaten.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You also stated that after the interrogation, you were sent to the pista.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did any of the interrogators send you to the pista?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The interrogator, in consultation with the guard who had brought me there, after they had finished said, "He has been interrogated. Take him to the pista."

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And my last question for you, Mr. Sivac: The guards or the guard, while you were at the pista and in Mujo's room, could they talk to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean, could the guards talk to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they could. They would take people out. They would call them by their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. So they were able to communicate with them freely?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call it exactly communication. It was rather rough treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I only wanted to know if they were free to do so on their own.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, witness. I have no further questions for you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Krstan Simic. Madam Hollis, is there going to be any redirect examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I haven't heard the interpretation, but I believe I have understood. I think that you don't have any questions for the witness. Judge Fouad Riad has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, good morning. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I would like to have some precisions concerning your testimony, and perhaps you may be in a position to help me. Concerning this incident of your being beaten by a whip with an iron end in it, and I won't describe it, by this guard called Savic -- by this guard called -- are you hearing me? Can you still hear me?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You were beaten by this guard called Savic till you fell on the stairs and so on. Was Radic in the vicinity in that case? Was he present? Because you also said that he would be always there when the gauntlet -- when you reached -- the whole group reached the gauntlet and would be giving orders for beatings. Was that under an order of Radic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he ordered that, but I know that he was at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the beginning of the gauntlet. Since it was in the shape of letter "L", it is quite probable that Mladjo Radic didn't see it happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: When he was there and things like that happened, did he order to prevent it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. He was probably inciting the guards to beat us even heart harder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Were you beaten by this Savic for any personal reason between you and him or were you just chosen as part of the whole group, as a systematic attitude?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quite systematic when it came to beatings. I had never seen Savic prior to my arrival in the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Speaking of some of the people you mentioned, you spoke about Kvocka. You said that he had always a soldier escorting him and standing behind him, behind his back. Was this a special treatment, or did many people have this privilege of being escorted and treated like that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The escort accompanied Miroslav Kvocka only when he was in the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And you mentioned concerning Krkan, you said that he would be calling people out, and they came back in bags or blankets, which is, of course, very clear. Was that especially the case with the people who Krkan called out, or was it also part of the systematic system, the systematic procedure of calling people out and the same - and coming back under the same conditions?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They conducted themselves in a systematic way. I spoke about the people who would come back from the interrogations in bags or blankets, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But you specified that it was especially in the case of Krkan?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the detainees were taken for interrogation, they were often killed in the interrogation rooms, during other shifts as well. It was not characteristic only of Krkan's shift.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So what made you say that, that it was more particularly in Krkan's shift? Was there something different? I have here your words.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was, because this took place most often in Krkan's shift.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that Krle would be seen also in the pista giving instructions to guards. Was it obvious that he was being obeyed and respected or just talking to them as one of them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One could observe that all of the orders that the guards had received from Krle would be implemented in respect of us -- would be implemented in respect of us. So it means that they did obey Krle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, speaking of Prcac, you said that he would give orders to the guards, especially to transfer detainees from one room to another. You mentioned to the Defence that he was specially -- or he was in charge of administrative affairs. But did you also watch or notice that he was commanding one of the shifts, or was he just an administrator?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not a shift commander. He would be in all of the shifts. He would even come to the camp during the night very often, and he would bring lists with names of detainees with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You also mentioned that most of the people who were called out were prominent citizens, those who went out and never came back. What did you mean by "prominent citizens"?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very respectable citizens: doctors, engineers, professors, economists, intellectuals, and other highly-respected people in the town of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And these were the people who were particularly called out?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Lastly, you went back, as you said, to Prijedor till the 16th of December, but you had to leave and left everything. You left your belongings, your savings, and everything. Did you really have to leave that, or was it because you just wanted to run away?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The pressure was enormous, and we had to abandon everything and try to save our lives and the lives of our family members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said you were under great pressure. They forced you to leave everything? Could you have gone out with your things with you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, we couldn't do that. We could only take some plastic bags with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And others accepted to stay and could stay, other people of your family, of your acquaintance?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My whole family who had been living in that town for 300 years had to abandon it; however, over 20 members of my close family were killed in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness Sivac. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Riad. Madam Judge Wald has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, do you know whether or not the interrogators were there all the time, or whether or not they came in the morning and went home at night, the interrogators?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came in a special bus to the Omarska camp at 8.00 in the morning, and they would leave after 5.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So there wouldn't be any -- to your knowledge, there wouldn't be any interrogators around in the evening hour after the bus left? Whatever happened in those later hours happened without the intervention or instruction of the interrogators; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: My next question is to clarify something that you said earlier. You said that toward the end of July there were more mass -- I think you used the word mass killings, callings out, things like that. Do I understand you correctly that things, conditions in the camp, got worse as time went by up until the very end, you said the two or two before, or is that not true? Did they stay the same, or did they get perceptively worse as time went by, from the time you came back on June 20, 23rd, whenever it was?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conditions in the camp were increasingly worse, and they reached the peak, I think, after the 20th of July. Then from the 20th of July, a number of people were called out and taken away, and those people never came back. It was especially intensive on the 25th, 26th, and the 27th of July. Those were the worst days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge or impression as to why that was so, why the number of callings out or disappearances would intensify at that period?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know, it is possible that the leadership, the people who had established the camps, hurried up and tried to liquidate all of their potential opponents, that is, the people who were likely to resist them upon their release. That is why during that period of time, almost all of the Prijedor intellectuals of Muslim and Croat ethnic background were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did this period follow any exposure of the existence of the camps in international or national media?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what they seemed to fear most, that the camps that they had established would be discovered, and that the images about the conditions in the camp would tour the world.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you knew Mr. Kvocka had a position of authority because he was treated with respect, and as he moved around he talked to the guards, the guards appeared to treat him with respect, to obey his orders. Let me ask you this question: On the first time that you were arrested, and you were only there for a short period on June 10th, and as I understand your testimony, Mr. Kvocka said, "Why are you here," and, "We'll have to talk to Mr. Meakic about this," and then ultimately you were released on that day. Then you came back on the 23rd, and you said you spent -- well, at one point you said the 23rd, another time around the 20th. But anyway, you spent seven days in the hangar, and then you would see Kvocka again when you went out on the pista in the first half of July. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. When you saw Mr. Kvocka in this second period, in the first half of July, was it your impression that he carried the same authority and respect and people treated him in the same way that they had treated him earlier when you saw him on June 10th? Do you see any reference in the way he was treated by the guards or in the appearance of his authority between the first time you saw him in early June and this period in the first part of July when you say you saw him several times on the pista?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could see, the relations didn't change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. My last question then would be: During this same period, the early part of July, you would see both Mr. Kvocka, I believe according to your testimony, and Mr. Prcac. Did you see any difference in the way they were treated or would you have said they had about the same authority, or would you say one had more authority than the other, Kvocka and Prcac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as one could observe, the treatment -- or rather, the authority was the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sivac, I have only one question for you. You have been answering questions by the Prosecutor, by the Defence, and the Judges. Is there anything else that you wish to say, anything that has not been said so far? If you wish to do so, you can do it now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much for providing me with the opportunity to testify before such an honourable Chamber. This was my moral obligation as a human being. All I wish to say at present is that during the events that took place in Prijedor in 1992, I lost countless friends as well, and I would like to say that I have been testifying here for the past two days on my behalf, in my own name, and I also felt that it was right for me to speak on their behalf as well. This is all that I wanted to say, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Sivac, for coming here to testify. We would like to wish you a pleasant journey back to your place of residence, and I hope that the thoughts that you have about the events that had taken place will help the world in a way and that the events -- such events will never happen again. I will now kindly ask the usher to show you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Hollis, what's the situation as regards our next witness? According to what I know, you requested certain protective measures for this witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before we proceed, let us think about the schedule. If we have a break now, then after that we will have one hour and 15 minutes for the testimony, for the examination. I should like to know whether it is worthwhile beginning with the testimony at all. I don't know whether we should begin the examination and then have a break until the 26th of August, without any contacts in the meantime. The witness will only have taken his oath and then the parties will not have an opportunity to contact the witness. I don't know what you think about that. I don't know whether we will be able to finish the examination, including the cross-examination within one hour and 15 minutes, because I'm referring to both stages of the examination of the witness. So if you think that it is possible, we can perhaps start, but if we do not have guarantees for that, and if the witness has to come back again after the 28th, I think it is better not to proceed with the witness. I should like to hear you, Ms. Hollis, on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, we don't think we could guarantee that we would finish the entire process. That being so, it is also the position of the Prosecutor that perhaps it would be better not to begin it without the ability to end it. We would be looking at approximately six weeks between the beginning of it and in finalising the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber thinks that we can at least make a ruling in respect of the protective measures for this witness. Pursuant to the oral request made by the Prosecutor yesterday, during a closed session hearing, with the objective of securing protective measures for the witness whose name was mentioned yesterday but whose name is not going to be mentioned now, the Chamber estimates that enough information has been supplied for us to grant the requested protective measures. For these reasons, the Chamber shall apply mutatis mutandis its oral ruling of the 3rd of May, 2000 and hereby grants the motion. The witness in question shall be given a pseudonym, pseudonym AN, and also shall benefit of protective measures involving face distortion. This has been our ruling. Before we adjourn, I should like to know if there is anything else that needs to be brought to our attention, anything that we did not discuss yesterday. We have a few minutes left, and we're now going to have a six-week break in this case. So if there is anything you should like to raise, this is the convenient time to do that. It seems that there are no issues to be discussed, so all I can do at this point is to wish you a nice holiday, if you can have one, and we will see each other again on the 28th of August to resume the trial in this case. Have a pleasant journey home, and I wish you a nice holiday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: 12.55 p.m. To be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of August, 2000 at 9.30 a.m.
